# Midwest AEC — Building Science & Architectural Specifications
> Authoritative technical specifications, cold-climate building physics, and contractor execution standards for Climate Zones 4 and 5 (IA, IL, IN, MI, MN, MO, ND, NE, OH, SD, WI).

Midwest AEC publishes peer-reviewed architectural and mechanical specifications covering moisture mitigation, foundation engineering, thermal boundaries, and cold-climate HVAC systems.

## Technical Specifications (Clean Markdown)
- [Attic Air Sealing & Eave Baffling: The Step-by-Step Cold Roof Retrofit](https://midwestaec.com/articles/attic-air-sealing-baffles.md): Attic air sealing and eave baffles stop winter ice dams permanently. Step-by-step guide to sealing top plate bypasses and installing R-60 under IECC R402.
- [The Attic Snow Cave: Diagnosing Winter Hoarfrost, Sweating Roof Sheathing & False Spring Leaks](https://midwestaec.com/articles/attic-frost-roof-sweating.md): Attic frost and sweating roof sheathing: Why bypass air leaks freeze into winter hoarfrost, and how to stop false spring ceiling leaks under IRC R806.
- [How to Firestop & Air-Seal Historic Balloon Framing: The Step-by-Step Retrofit](https://midwestaec.com/articles/balloon-framing-retrofit-steps.md): How to firestop balloon framing: Step-by-step retrofit guide to installing mineral wool blocks and intumescent mastic to stop chimney drafts under IRC R302.
- [Balloon Framing Air Leaks: How to Firestop and Seal the Chimney Effect in Pre-1940s Homes](https://midwestaec.com/articles/balloon-framing.md): Balloon framing air leaks act as open chimneys in pre-1940s homes. Learn how to air-seal open stud bays and install code-approved IRC R302.11 firestops.
- [Barndominium & Post-Frame Thermal Envelopes: Zone 5 Condensation Control](https://midwestaec.com/articles/barndominium-post-frame.md): Barndominium insulation and condensation control: How to detail continuous outboard foam and ventilated rainscreens to prevent rotting posts under IBC 1404.
- [Legal Basement Finishing: Cutting Egress Windows in Poured Concrete, IRC R310 Codes & Slab Framing](https://midwestaec.com/articles/basement-egress-window-cutting.md): Turning an unfinished basement into a legal bedroom or recreation room is the highest-ROI square footage addition in the Midwest. But building inspectors will red-tag any space without code-compliant emergency egress. We break down IRC Section R310 dimensions (5.7 sq ft net clear opening), diamond wet sawing through 8-inch reinforced concrete, structural steel lintel sizing, and why connecting window well drains to perimeter footing tiles prevents basement floods.
- [Why '100% Waterproof' Basement LVP Flooring Fails: Sub-Slab Vapor Pressure, MVER & Concrete Condensation](https://midwestaec.com/articles/basement-lvp-flooring-moisture.md): Basement LVP flooring moisture: Why waterproof vinyl buckles over concrete slabs, and how to test MVER under ASTM F1869 with Class A vapor retarders.
- [Why Water Enters Midwest Basements After Heavy Rain: Hydrostatic Head and Under-Slab Vapor Barriers](https://midwestaec.com/articles/basement-waterproofing.md): Basement waterproofing after heavy rain: How expansive clay funnels hydrostatic head pressure through cove joints, and the ASTM E1745 Class A barrier fix.
- [How to Pass the Blower Door Test (< 3.0 ACH50) on a Midwest Remodel](https://midwestaec.com/articles/blower-door-checklist.md): Pass the blower door test on your remodel: A contractor checklist for hitting < 3.0 ACH50 under IECC R402.4 by air-sealing top plates and rim joists.
- [Rural Bug & Pest Prevention: Termite Shields, Carpenter Ants & Perimeter Envelopes](https://midwestaec.com/articles/bug-prevention.md): Pest prevention starts at the building envelope: How air-sealing rim joists, weep screens, and sill gaskets stops insects and termites under IRC P2605.
- [Can a Heat Pump Actually Handle -15°F? Cold-Climate Inverters During Midwest Winters](https://midwestaec.com/articles/cold-climate-heat-pumps.md): Cold-climate heat pumps at -20°F: How inverter vapor-injection and R744 transcritical cycles eliminate electric strips and cut winter heating bills in Zone 5.
- [Continuous Exterior Insulation: Why R-5 Outboard Beats R-20 Cavity in Freeze-Thaw Climates](https://midwestaec.com/articles/continuous-insulation.md): Continuous exterior insulation on 2x6 walls: Calculate dew point planes, prevent sheathing condensation, and eliminate thermal bridging under IRC R702.
- [How to Encapsulate a Crawl Space: The Step-by-Step Conversion Guide](https://midwestaec.com/articles/crawlspace-encapsulation-steps.md): How to do crawl space encapsulation under IRC R408.3: Step-by-step contractor manual for 20-mil Class A liners, exterior vent sealing, and commercial dehumidification.
- [Crawlspace Encapsulation vs. Open Venting in the Midwest: Mold, Odors & Heating Costs](https://midwestaec.com/articles/crawlspace-encapsulation.md): Crawl space encapsulation vs vented dirt floors: Why 20-mil sealed liners and commercial dehumidifiers cut floor rot and mold risk under IRC Section R408.
- [Does an Old House Need to Breathe? The Building Science of Stack Pressure, Infiltration Rot & ERVs](https://midwestaec.com/articles/does-house-need-to-breathe.md): Does a house need to breathe? The building science truth behind controlled mechanical ventilation (ERV/HRV) vs uncontrolled wall rot under ASHRAE 62.2.
- [Spray Foam vs. Cellulose & Wood Fiber: Why Plastic Foam Traps Moisture, Rots Studs & Fails the 25-Year Payback](https://midwestaec.com/articles/embodied-carbon-materials.md): Spray foam vs cellulose insulation: Closed-cell foam creates non-breathable vapor dams that rot wood studs in Climate Zone 5, while dense-pack cellulose and wood fiber provide vapor-open moisture buffering and net-negative carbon footprints.
- [Winter Tariff Hikes: Why $20k on Windows Doesn't Hold Up](https://midwestaec.com/articles/energy-hikes.md): Winter utility rate hikes: How air-sealing attic bypasses and setting heat pump balance points protects homeowners against 20–40% Midwest rate surges.
- [Expansive Lawncare & Acreage Grading: Swales, Prairie Buffers & Soil Drainage](https://midwestaec.com/articles/expansive-lawncare.md): Expansive clay soils and foundation cracking: How seasonal moisture swings cause basement settlement, and the soaker hose watering rule to prevent cracks.
- [The False Spring Thaw: Why Your Attic Rains, Your Basement Sweats, and Your Winter Bills Spiked](https://midwestaec.com/articles/false-spring-envelope-thaw.md): False spring freeze-thaw cycles: How 50°F daytime thaws and sub-zero nights tear gutters, crack masonry, and cause hidden ceiling leaks in Climate Zone 5.
- [How to Safely Insulate Historic Solid Brick: The Interior Retrofit Blueprint](https://midwestaec.com/articles/historic-brick-retrofit-steps.md): How to insulate historic brick walls safely: Step-by-step interior retrofit detailing 2-inch continuous smart vapor retarders and lime mortar repointing.
- [How to Know If You Need an ICF Basement: The 6-Point Inspection Checklist & When to Retrofit](https://midwestaec.com/articles/how-to-know-if-you-need-icf-basement.md): Unfinished Midwest basements tell clear visual stories if you know what to look for. From horizontal mortar cracks caused by expanding clay soil to white chalky efflorescence and freezing perimeter walls, we break down the 6-point DIY basement inspection checklist. Learn when an existing home warrants an ICF addition or replacement, how monolithic concrete eliminates moisture intrusion, and why structural diagnostics always require licensed professional verification.
- [The Physics of Midwest Ice Dams: The Real Fix (And Why Heat Cables Don't Work)](https://midwestaec.com/articles/ice-dams-roofs.md): Ice dams on roofs: The thermodynamic physics of attic heat loss, and how continuous air-sealing and ice-and-water shield prevent gutter dam roof leaks.
- [ICF (Insulated Concrete Forms) for Midwest Basements: Eliminating Moisture & Freezing Walls](https://midwestaec.com/articles/icf-basements-walls.md): ICF basement foundations deliver continuous R-22+ insulation with zero moisture wicking. Compare poured concrete vs. insulated concrete forms cost and IRC R404 specs.
- [Insulating 100-Year-Old Brick Homes: Freeze-Thaw Spalling and Interior Vapor Retarders](https://midwestaec.com/articles/insulating-brick.md): Clay insulating brick retrofits: Why interior insulation causes historic brick spalling in sub-zero winters, and the hygrothermal blueprint to do it safely.
- [Rural Off-Grid Systems in Zone 5: Propane, Battery Backup & Freeze-Proof Wells](https://midwestaec.com/articles/off-grid-systems.md): Off-grid solar and battery storage in Zone 5: How to size LiFePO4 batteries and low-temperature inverters to survive 5 straight days of sub-zero cloud cover.
- [The Midwest Rammed Earth Paradox: Thermal Mass, Freeze-Thaw Spalling & The Sub-Slab Flooring Matrix](https://midwestaec.com/articles/rammed-earth-midwest-flooring.md): Rammed earth and earthen floors in Zone 5: Why uninsulated earth provides only R-3.6, and how to detail Stabilized Insulated Rammed Earth (SIRE) under IRC R402.
- [Does Rockwool Outperform Fiberglass? How Each Holds Up in Midwest Wall Assemblies](https://midwestaec.com/articles/rockwool-vs-fiberglass.md): Rockwool vs. fiberglass insulation: Compare R-values (R-4.2 vs R-3.2), fire resistance, soundproofing, and sub-zero convective derating in Midwest walls.
- [Adding Continuous Insulation When Replacing Your Roof: Over-Sheathing Cathedral Ceilings](https://midwestaec.com/articles/roof-insulation-over-sheathing.md): Roof insulation over sheathing: How adding continuous rigid polyiso or stone wool above cathedral rafters stops ice dams and cuts drafts under IRC R806.5.
- [SIPs (Structural Insulated Panels) in Zone 5: Total Cost vs. Traditional Stick Framing](https://midwestaec.com/articles/sips-vs-traditional-framing.md): SIPs vs. traditional stick framing in Zone 5: Compare total build costs, sub-1.0 ACH50 airtightness, crane labor savings, and HVAC downsizing under IRC R610.
- [Smart Vapor Retarders vs. 6-Mil Plastic: Why Polyethylene Traps Mold in Midwest Summers](https://midwestaec.com/articles/smart-vapor-retarders.md): Smart vapor retarders vs. 6-mil plastic: Why polyethylene traps summer mold behind drywall, and how variable-perm membranes breathe under IRC Section R702.7.
- [Below-Slab and Rim Joist Foam Spec: Stopping Frost-Heave and Basement Heat Loss](https://midwestaec.com/articles/sub-slab-insulation-specs.md): Below grade insulation & sub-slab specs: ASTM E1745 Class A vapor retarders, ASTM E1643 installation practice, and high-density Type IX EPS vs XPS under ASTM C578.
- [The Midwest Summer Humidity Trap: Why High-Efficiency AC Leaves Your Basement Cold & Clammy](https://midwestaec.com/articles/summer-humidity-ac.md): Oversized AC and basement humidity: Why short-cycling high-efficiency air conditioners leave rooms cold and clammy, and how to fix SHR under ACCA Manual S.
- [When Replacing Windows Actually Makes Sense (And What Specifications to Demand)](https://midwestaec.com/articles/when-to-replace-windows.md): When to replace windows: 4 structural failure triggers that justify the 30-year payback. How to diagnose blown IGU seals and fix drafty frames for 1/4 the cost.
